newsitem.title: USA: TWA unions brace for layoffs at Kennedy.
newsitem.headline: TWA unions brace for layoffs at Kennedy.

text.p: Unions representing Trans World Airlines Inc's mechanics and flight attendants are warning members that the airline may lay off more than 700 people at Kennedy International Airport in New York by February 1.

According to a recorded message on an International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers' hotline, 509 union members may be laid off, including 241 customer service representatives, 245 ramp workers and 23 guards.
"Hopefully the layoffs will not reach these projected numbers," the December 30 message said, adding that the airline was still reviewing operational changes at Kennedy.
TWA, the nation's seventh-largest airline, said last month it was discussing plans to stem losses on its trans-Atlantic flights, and layoffs at Kennedy would be part of the program.

"The numbers quoted by the machinists' union are a worst-case scenario included in a (federally required layoff notice) TWA issued December 20," John McDonald, a spokesman for the St. Louis-based airline, said Friday. "The actual number (of job cuts) has not been determined."

Barry Schimmel, secretary and treasurer of the Independent Federation of Flight Attendants, said Friday he was told that 195 flight attendants could be laid off at Kennedy this month. He said the company was planning a "larger-than-normal winter pull-down of its schedule as marketing and business plans changed."

"We are working with TWA to minimize the number of involuntary layoffs," Schimmel said. The union is scheduled to hold a conference call with TWA officials Monday afternoon to discuss operational changes at the airport, Schimmel said.

TWA has about 6,200 employees at Kennedy, McDonald said. He added that the three-year labor contracts with TWA's union pilots, machinists and flight attendants are all scheduled to expire "in the first part of September."
The company's stock closed up 7/16 Friday at 7-5/16.
